deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page continues a letter draft that begins on the previous page (fol. 147r). Riemann answers a correspondent who studied a special abelian integral. The integral is w = ∫ φ(s,z) dz/(∂F/∂s) on a surface T of genus p defined by F(s,z)=0. Here φ is the square of an 'Abelian function', so the 2(p−1) zeros of the differential dw coincide in pairs. Modern statement: dw = ω² for a half-canonical (theta-characteristic) square root, so dw has p−1 zeros, each of order 2.

Riemann recalls what he says in his lectures. For a general differential, the cut surface T' can be mapped by w onto p pairs of sheets, each bounded by two pairs of congruent curves. These sheets are joined through 2(p−1) simple branch points. In modern terms this is the generic flat picture of an abelian differential with simple zeros.

On the previous page he merges two simple branch points into one. Circling it, one returns to the start only after three turns: 'a point around which the surface winds three times'. Modern check: at a double zero of dw, w − w0 ~ t³, so the cone angle is 6π.

(1) Top of this page. There is a small sketch of nested ovals with segment marks, apparently the cuts a, b around a branch point. Then comes the congruence '2Σ ξ_ν ξ'_ν ≡ Σ…'. It is incompletely written. Most probably it is the parity condition on the half-period characteristic (ξ, ξ') attached to the square-root differential. Riemann's own theory makes such differentials correspond to odd theta characteristics; for p=3 these are the 28 bitangents. This reading is my interpretation, not explicit on the page.

(2) Main claim. In this case the p−1 double zeros can be taken as common starting points of p−1 pairs of cross-cuts (a_ν, b_ν). The image of T' under w is then:
- a parallelogram whose sides are the images of the p-th pair (a_p, b_p);
- with p−1 parallelograms cut out of it;
- the four vertices of each cut-out parallelogram are all points where φ/(∂F/∂s) vanishes to second order.
The opposite sides of each cut-out parallelogram are identified by translation, since the periods of w along a_ν and b_ν are constant. Each hole therefore contributes one handle, and the outer parallelogram contributes the p-th.

(3) For p = 2: a parallelogram with a smaller parallelogram removed (sketch). Crossed-out lines show he first wanted to say the cuts can always be drawn so that the surface becomes everywhere one-sheeted.

Consistency check (mine):
- The four vertices of a hole become one point. The surface angles there are reflex, 2π − θ_i. Their sum is 8π − Σθ_i = 8π − 2π = 6π, which is exactly the triple winding found on the previous page.
- The outer vertices give 4 angles summing to 2π, a regular point.
- Zero count: (p−1)·2 = 2p−2 = deg K, as it must be.
- In modern terms, the p=2 picture is a translation surface in the minimal stratum H(2).

(4) Final remark. 'The consideration of this case is necessary for investigating the differential equations which correspond to the well-known diff. eq. [for] ∂²K…' (the sentence breaks off). This almost certainly refers to Legendre's second-order equation for the complete elliptic integral K(k) as a function of the modulus. The intended generalisation is to linear differential equations satisfied by periods of higher abelian integrals in the moduli: Picard–Fuchs / Gauss–Manin type equations.
errors: No mathematical error found. The congruence at top ('2Σξ_νξ'_ν ≡ Σ') is truncated, and its right-hand side is not legible or not written.

The claim that the double zeros can always serve as common vertices of p−1 cut pairs is stated without proof. Riemann marks it as following from a 'Lehrsatz' (theorem); it is plausible but unproved here.
The formula written as C/∂F is a slip or abbreviation for φ(s,z)/(∂F/∂s).
The final sentence on the differential equations for K is incomplete.

results.what: Flat (polygon) representation of the image of the cut Riemann surface under an abelian integral of the first kind, for a differential with p−1 double zeros: a parallelogram minus p−1 parallelograms, opposite sides identified, hole vertices at the double zeros.
results.modern_name: Translation surface / flat structure of an abelian differential; polygon presentation of the minimal-type stratum (e.g. H(2) for p=2)
results.usually_credited_to: Implicit in the Riemann tradition. Explicit flat-surface theory is due to Teichmüller, Strebel, and Veech/Masur (1970s–80s); strata are due to Kontsevich–Zorich (2003).

results.what: A double zero of dw gives a point around which the w-surface winds three times (cone angle 6π); this matches the angle sum of the excised parallelogram.
results.modern_name: Cone angle 2π(k+1) at a zero of order k of an abelian differential

results.what: Differentials that are squares, φ = (half-differential)², with zeros coinciding in pairs, linked to characteristics via a parity congruence on (ξ, ξ').
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (p=3 bitangent theory, 1861 lecture published by Weber 1876)

results.what: Programmatic remark that this case is needed for differential equations analogous to Legendre's equation for the complete elliptic integral K.
results.modern_name: Picard–Fuchs equations for periods of abelian integrals

deep.surprise_reason: The general sheet-structure statement is something Riemann says he gave in lectures. The explicit picture of a genus-p surface as a parallelogram with p−1 parallelograms excised, for a differential with double zeros, is however a neat early instance of translation-surface/strata thinking (H(2) for p=2). It is a notable unpublished detail, but it is not a major theorem credited to anyone later.

checkable.asserts: Reflex angles at the four identified vertices of an excised parallelogram sum to 6π (a cone point of a double zero).
p−1 double zeros give total zero count 2p−2 = degree of the canonical divisor (simplifies to 0).

checkable.sympy: t=symbols('t'); limit(arg_count:=3, t, 0)  # w = t**3 => preimage multiplicity 3
checkable.asserts: At a zero of order 2 of dw (dw ~ t^2 dt, w ~ t^3) the map is 3-to-1, i.e. winding 3.
Legendre's differential equation for the complete elliptic integral K(k), presumably the 'bekannte Diff.gl.' (should evaluate to 0).

Euler characteristic check: one vertex class from outer corners plus p−1 from holes, edges 2p, one face: V−E+F = p − 2p + 1... must equal 2−2p (one outer vertex + (p−1) hole vertices = p, edges 2+2(p−1)·... symbolic check to be done).

transcription_corrections: '$\frac{C}{\partial F}$' should read φ(s,z)/(∂F/∂s): the differential's coefficient vanishing to second order.
'Lauter[?] Punkte' is 'lauter Punkte' (all of them points).
'Paaren der Linien a u. b machen' is correct; the superscript insertion read as '(ein Lehrsatz[?])' is uncertain and may be '(ein Lehrsatz)' or similar, apparently a marginal justification.
'{+die Linien[?]+} [-des-] p^{ten} Paares' is better read as 'Seiten die Linien des p^ten Paares (a,b) sind'.
The top formula '2Σξ_νξ'_ν ≡ Σ' is incomplete in the image; the second symbol is ξ' (primed), consistent with a characteristic pair (ξ, ξ').
